chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, who said:
I asked him about a man who performed ghusl before urinating, so he wrote: the ghusl is after urination, unless he had forgotten; then he does not repeat the ghusl because of it.
So this report came clarifying all the hadiths in the manner that we mentioned: that this applies specifically to one who left it out forgetfully.

As for what is contained in the report of Samāʿah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim mentioning the repetition of wudu (ablution), it is to be understood as recommended. And it is possible that what is meant by what came out after urination and ghusl is that which invalidates wudu (ablution); in that case wudu (ablution) becomes obligatory upon him. For that reason he, peace be upon him, said, 'He must perform wudu (ablution) and istinjāʾ,' in the hadith of Samāʿah, and that only applies to what invalidates wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal application
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urination before ghusl as part of istibrāʾ from janabah

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl have to be repeated if someone performed it before urinating after janabah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of performing ghusl after urinating in the context of janabah, and clarifies that if a person omitted urination forgetfully, he does not have to repeat the ghusl. It also explains that narrations mentioning repeating wudu (ablution) are either understood as recommended or as applying when something exits that actually invalidates wudu (ablution).
